proposed_from.topic: Dual co-main contribution for Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu distance-based boundary estimation. First, on the exact P_NP(L,q) law class for integer q >= 1 and L >= 4, prove the (log n/n)^(1/4) lower bound for arbitrary law-independent point-indexed Borel sections and hence for the literal displayed CTY common-map class; this full-P_NP result is converse-only and claims no full-class achievability. Second, on the distinct exact displayed L-uniformized Euclidean-distance, uniform-kernel CTY Assumptions 1–2 plus Theorem-2-envelope class P12(p,nu,L), retain the explicit winsorized Gram-stabilized expected-risk upper for L >= 4 and the matched outer-expected minimax frontier for L >= L0(p). Position the P12 theorem as a separate co-main result: CTY provide identification, sequence-scoped bias, and probability-order stochastic control but do not state this common-law-class outer-expected minimax equality. Do not claim broader metric/kernel coverage, exact constants, or transfer of the P12 upper to full P_NP.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The first advance is a matching logarithmic converse and degree-zero upper bound on an explicitly defined primitive rectifiable class, not a same-class claim about the anchor's nonparametric class. The second is a geometry-saturation theorem: smooth embedded boundaries and smooth outcome regressions do not improve the uniform coordinatewise-distance frontier over bounded continuous densities without a shared modulus. The third holds the straight assignment design and law class fixed while separating the distance-only and full-location minimax exponents. None of the named comparators provides this three-part frontier.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected seed survives four adjacent checks. First, CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance, Theorem 6 and its supplemental proof, uses one angular-support pair with radial Kullback--Leibler divergence of order \(s^4\); the proof ends with a two-point Le Cam choice \(s\asymp n^{-1/4}\), so it does not contain the multi-location logarithm. Second, Stone1982OptimalGlobal establishes the full-location sup-norm logarithmic benchmark but has no point-specific distance channel. Third, ChenChristensen2018SupNorm, proof of its minimax lower theorem, selects many disjoint interior wavelets and applies Tsybakov multiple testing with divergence bounded by a constant times the logarithm of packing cardinality; this is the estimator-construction exemplar adapted to boundary charts. Fourth, AamariAaronLevrard2021Boundary, Sections on lower-bound tools and hypotheses with boundary, perturbs smooth embedded supports through controlled diffeomorphisms while preserving reach and density envelopes; this is the geometry exemplar for the smooth converse. CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Survey is the recent field survey and reveals no closer converse. For the deferred adaptive candidate, Bull2012SelfSimilarBands proves self-similarity is essentially necessary for honest continuous-smoothness adaptation, HoffmannNickl2011AdaptiveBands gives separation-based adaptation, and ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference limits data-dependent tightening over convex classes. For the deferred regularization candidate, AamariAaronLevrard2021Boundary and BickelLi2007ManifoldLPR provide boundary reconstruction and intrinsic local-polynomial tools, but a regularized causal target must first be chosen. No searched paper subsumes the selected coordinatewise distance-channel kernel.
